title: Proximity-weighted admission with circuit-breaker cascades
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Goal: implement a hierarchical, proximity-weighted admission controller that combines latency-based routing, geo-pin affinity, and capacity-aware steering with progressive circuit-breaker cascades and soft eviction. This ticket covers design, a reference implementation in the router, telemetry hooks, and a controlled rollout. Background: recent multi-region incidents showed blind hedging causes cache misses and client-level amplification. We need an admission policy that: (1) prioritizes regional affinity for cold-cache/low-cost traffic, (2) admits a tunable fraction of cross-region hedges when local capacity or latency SLOs threaten, and (3) applies cascading breakers that degrade gracefully rather than binary ejection. Key idea: compute a proximity weight per request (customer pin + geo score + latency budget headroom + model cost factor) and use that weight to decide admission into local vs remote pools and to allocate ephemeral admission tokens from region-capacity windows. When capacity windows are scarce, activate circuit-breaker cascades with decaying penalties (soft-eject percentage, increased hedging timeout, and incremental retry backoff) instead of immediate 100% shedding. Runtime signals: per-region token bucket, 95th/99th tail latency windows, KV-cache hit ratio, GPU queue depth, and autoscaler target states. SLO mapping: map token admission thresholds to specific SLOs (latency p95 < X ms -> preserve admission; p95 > X ms -> progressively shed non-pinned weights).
telemetry_requirements: emit region:latency_p95, region:latency_p99, region:queue_depth, region:admission_tokens_used, request:proximity_weight, request:hedge_taken, customer:pin_status, model:kv_cache_hit_rate
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for admission decision functions and token-window accounting
Integration test injecting synthetic region load and verifying progressive soft-eviction percentages
Dashboard with heatmaps for proximity_weight distribution and per-region token consumption
Canary rollout plan and rollback flag implementated
Documentation: design doc, ops runbook, and public changelog notes
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Disabled by default. Run traffic shadowing in staging and capture decisions for 48h
Stage 2: Enable for 1% traffic in us-west-2 for non-critical tenants for 72h, observe token usage and tail latency
Stage 3: Expand to 10% across multi-regions with tightened telemetry alarms
Stage 4: Enable by default with gradual ramp and enable soft-fence thresholds configurable per-customer tier
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff synced with Routing and Serving runtime teams. Agreed scope to start with model-serving paths only.

2026-03-05: Prototype of proximity_weight computed (pin: 0/1, geo_score 0..1, latency_headroom scaled -1..1, model_cost factor). Early trade-off: include kv_cache_hit as multiplier increases variance; decided to surface as optional multiplier for first pass.
2026-03-08: UX asked for admin override per-customer; added per-customer golden-path token pool to design.
2026-03-10: Security review flagged telemetry containing customer pin; agreed to hash customer IDs and use role-based access to dashboards.
2026-03-12: Initial router prototype in branch ready for integration test. Perf note: decision code adds ~120ns median; acceptable after inlining and benchmark.

2026-03-13: Ops ran synthetic overload test; cascade breakers correctly reduced non-pinned admission to 40% over 5 minutes and recovered when load subsided. Found edge-case where hedged requests doubled backend load during scale-up; mitigation: time-jitter hedges and limit concurrent hedges per region.
risks: Hedging plus cross-region admission may amplify scale-up loops if autoscaler lags. Also, incorrect proximity weight tuning could bias small customers. Mitigations: conservative defaults, canary, autoscaler coordination signals, and bounded concurrent hedges per-customer.
remaining_tasks: finish integration test harness, add per-customer golden pool config UI, implement telemetry hashing, add automated rollback alarm in mission-control, and write ops runbook
